# avahi / fuzz-consume-record

avahi's own fuzz target `fuzz-consume-record` ([source](source/fuzz-consume-record.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over avahi (avahi/avahi at b1a83592).

Checks 6 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: rdata serialize -> avahi_rdata_parse into a fresh record with the same name/class/type/ttl -> avahi_record_equal_no_ttl(original, reparsed) must hold (type-aware full rdata equality). A re-parse FAILURE is not flagged (goto finish).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against avahi at commit b1a83592.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- a record parsed from the packet (avahi_dns_packet_consume_record) must satisfy avahi_record_is_valid ([lines 56-57](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L56-L57)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- the rdata of any successfully parsed record must serialize into an AVAHI_DNS_RDATA_MAX buffer without error ([lines 67-72](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L67-L72)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- rdata serialize -> avahi_rdata_parse into a fresh record with the same name/class/type/ttl -> avahi_record_equal_no_ttl(original, reparsed) must hold (type-aware full rdata equality). A re-parse FAILURE is not flagged (goto finish) ([lines 77-84](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L77-L84)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- the re-parsed record must satisfy avahi_record_is_valid ([lines 80-81](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L80-L81)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.
- second comparator on the same roundtrip: avahi_record_lexicographical_compare(original, reparsed) == 0 (under #ifndef HAVE_NALLOCFUZZ, i.e. live by default) ([lines 86-88](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L86-L88)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- avahi_record_copy(r) must be equal_no_ttl to r and lexicographically compare 0 against it ([lines 94-99](source/fuzz-consume-record.c#L94-L99)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failure of any of the checks at lines 67-72, lines 86-88 and lines 94-99 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name them exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies them on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

| statement | in one line | status |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at lines 67-72, lines 86-88 and lines 94-99 above hold | open |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at lines 67-72, lines 86-88 and lines 94-99 above hold | open |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires | open |
| `ubsan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and UBSan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `ubsan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and UBSan agree | open |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch avahi` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz-consume-record.plain` | 71,536 | `dc1d905e95da28aa61bcc3cec71906c3b6159bfab0514084ab485aed74450a7a` |
| ubsan | `fuzz-consume-record.ubsan` | 73,632 | `58d26d58330bd9b1c25c4906bfe9ac0bcbca4c29b617cd3020e56dc573044b20` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
